clue.text: Step out of line going behind a bishop’s residence

indicators.note: to go behind something is to follow it, so one piece is placed after another
a word stretched out around others is spread so it surrounds them

blocks.note: a pace is a single step
taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone stepping out of line on their way behind a bishop's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going behind' reads as sneaking around, but it only orders two small pieces; 'out of' then has the step stretch round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's official home is traditionally called his palace, as at Lambeth or Wells.

clue.text: Unexpected difficulty in autumn match at the outset

indicators.note: something at the outset comes at the very start, so this piece leads the answer

blocks.note: to pit one side against another is to match them
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A surprise problem cropping up in an autumn fixture's opening stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' reads as a noun, a game, but here it is the verb: to pit opponents against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or trap, literally a concealed pit, so a problem that catches you unawares.

clue.text: Extreme source of loving? That’s me!

indicators.note: the source of something is where it begins, so only its opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of loving
the cry of the chaser in the playground game of tag: I'm it!

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that they are the ultimate in affection.
explanation.walkthrough: In tag the player who must chase is 'it', so 'That's me!' is spoken as I'M IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An extreme is the furthest point anything can reach, its outermost boundary or end point.

clue.text: Fish will encompass article frequently upheld … as this?

definitions.text: Fish will encompass article frequently upheld … as this?

indicators.note: held up in a down entry, the word reads from bottom to top
to encompass is to surround, so one piece goes around the rest

blocks.note: the cod is a common food fish
the indefinite article
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A fish, often lifted up and offered, ends up as pet food.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: cod is exactly the kind of fish that goes into tins for cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish such as cod is a staple ingredient of tinned meals sold for feeding pet cats.

clue.text: Change that is following description of requirements

indicators.note: what is following comes next in line, so this piece sits after the other

blocks.note: a spec, short for specification, sets out what is required
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: A revision made after a list of needs was drawn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like alteration, but it is loose change: coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is money in coin form rather than notes, and coins are what we call change.

clue.text: A note kept in seventh enclosure in part of Malaysia

indicators.note: whatever is kept in something is held inside it

blocks.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
G is the seventh letter of the alphabet
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A message tucked away inside the seventh compound somewhere in Malaysia.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece is built in an unusual order: enclosure then seventh gives PEN-G, and AN slips between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Penang is an island state on the northwest coast of peninsular Malaysia, home to George Town.

clue.text: Underwater work environment? Department supporting bid to block river

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so this piece comes after
a blockage sits inside a channel, so these letters go within

blocks.note: a bid is an offer at auction
D is the abbreviation for department
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A bureaucratic department backs an attempt to dam a river for an undersea workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a playful description: the work takes place below water level, not in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cofferdam is a watertight enclosure pumped dry so builders can work on foundations below the waterline.

clue.text: Old Queen number in risqué setting? It’s going wrong

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel inside it, so one piece is mounted within the other

blocks.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
racy means slightly indecent
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: An old queen performing a saucy song in a bawdy show, and it all goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' here is the abbreviation, not a song; 'setting' tells you the racy word holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Errancy is the condition of erring, straying from what is right or making mistakes.

clue.text: ‘Coo’ and ‘moo’ with patient working out may be considered thus?

definitions.text: ‘Coo’ and ‘moo’ with patient working out may be considered thus?

indicators.note: working something out means solving it by rearranging its parts

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient thinker works out how to classify words like coo and moo.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: coo and moo really are words that imitate the sounds they name.
explanation.definitionFit: Onomatopoeic words imitate the noise they describe, like a dove's coo or a cow's moo.

clue.text: Source of cash containing nothing? A tiny amount

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: an ATM is a cash machine
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: An empty cash machine offers only a pittance.
explanation.walkthrough: ATM, automated teller machine, is the cash dispenser in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest particle of matter, so figuratively the merest scrap or trace of something.

clue.text: One car’s last away from two junctions – take note from this

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only
what is taken away from something is removed from it

blocks.note: the final letter of car
a turning and a fork are both junctions in a road

explanation.surface: A lone driver loses their way between two road junctions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' simply means a single letter: the one R of car goes from TURNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuning fork rings at a fixed pitch, so musicians take their reference note from it.

clue.text: Military display that’s equally rubbish?

blocks.note: tat is cheap junk
too means also, likewise

explanation.surface: A sneer at a parade that is just as much rubbish as everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads backwards from the surface: 'equally rubbish' becomes rubbish, then equally.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an evening military pageant with marching bands, as at the Edinburgh Tattoo.

clue.text: Bloke, uncommon gent, foremost in art?

definitions.text: Bloke, uncommon gent, foremost in art?

indicators.note: something uncommon is unusual, out of its normal form, so letters are rearranged
the foremost part is at the very front, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: a bloke is a man
taken as written
the first letter of art

explanation.surface: Praise for a remarkable man who leads the field in painting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: an uncommon man who was foremost in art.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Mantegna was a leading Italian Renaissance painter, celebrated for bold perspective and frescoes in Mantua.

clue.text: Clarify cryptic clue I’d put away

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
to put food away is to eat it

explanation.surface: A solver asking to have a cryptic clue explained before giving up on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' is informal for eating, past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to make something clear by explaining it, a formal synonym of clarify.

clue.text: So over getting upset amidst dubious ethics, becoming selective in the extreme

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, reading bottom to top
something dubious is unreliable and not in proper order
amidst means in the middle of, so these letters sit inside

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone upset by shady morals grows extremely fussy about whom they deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the anagram signal but, in a down clue, it turns the short piece upside down; 'dubious' does the jumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Choosiest is the superlative of choosy, meaning most particular or fussy in making choices.

clue.text: Clearly losing verses about Italy without much effort

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other
what a word is losing is taken out of it

blocks.note: vividly means clearly, distinctly
v is the abbreviation for verse, doubled for plural
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A poet dashing off lines about Italy with little effort, and it shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Vs wrap the I to make VIV, which comes off the front of VIVIDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something idly means lazily or in a relaxed way, putting little energy into it.

clue.text: Hail beauty, without one love recalled

indicators.note: to go without is to lack, so letters are taken away
to be called back is to go the way you came

blocks.note: good looks are beauty
love is zero in tennis, written O; one of the two is dropped

explanation.surface: A greeting to a former beauty queen whose lover has been recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: LOOKS loses just one of its two Os before turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Skol is a Scandinavian drinking toast, and hail is a cry of greeting or salute.

clue.text: Forerunner of reggae insufficiently succinct for ice dancers?

indicators.note: insufficient means falling short, so the word stops before its end

blocks.note: ska, Jamaican music of the 1960s, preceded reggae
terse means brief and to the point

explanation.surface: Old Jamaican music too short-winded for figure skating routines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forerunner' wants to be a first letter, R; here it is the whole genre that came before reggae.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice dancing is a skating discipline, so its performers are skaters, an example-based definition flagged by the question mark.

clue.text: Southern fruit not used for flavouring

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a pear is a fruit
in mint condition means unused, as new

explanation.surface: Fruit from the South that goes unused when choosing a flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not used' looks like a negative instruction, but it is a description: mint, as in mint condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a species of mint widely used to flavour chewing gum, toothpaste and sweets.

clue.text: Police action limiting my support for member

indicators.note: a limit is a boundary on both sides, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: police make arrests
my is shortened to m' in forms such as m'lady and m'lud

explanation.surface: A police operation restricting someone backed by a Member of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests an MP; it is a limb, here the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: An armrest supports a person's arm, and a limb such as an arm is a member of the body.

clue.text: Knight’s article penetrating cloth

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
the indefinite article
a penetrating mind is keen, sharp

explanation.surface: A knight's sharp lance piercing fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penetrating' looks like an instruction to insert one piece into another; it is just the adjective keen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric originally made in Nanjing, China, used for trousers.

clue.text: Ant, sir, represented insect form

indicators.note: to be represented is to be shown in a different form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone addressing an ant politely as it is drawn as a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sir' reads as a form of address, but it is only letters to be rearranged with ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An instar is a developmental stage of an insect between two successive moults of its exoskeleton.

clue.text: European city with way to keep America neutralised at outset

indicators.note: the outset is the very start, so only the first letter is kept
to keep something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: a lane is a narrow road or way
the United States of America
the opening letter of neutralised

explanation.surface: A European city whose roads hold back an America defused from the start, apt for neutral Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neutralised at outset' is not an action on America; it supplies one letter that joins USA inside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Lausanne is a city in French-speaking Switzerland on Lake Geneva, home of the Olympic committee.

clue.text: Sheep farmer not distant in ring

indicators.note: not means without, so the following word is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
far means distant
taken as written
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A sheep farmer who stays close by in the show ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheep farmer' reads as one phrase; only the first word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The merino is a breed of sheep prized for its very fine, soft wool.

clue.text: Unpleasant look climbing round top of peak? Turn back

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter
climbing in a down entry means reading upwards, bottom to top
round means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a leer is a nasty, suggestive look
the opening letter of peak

explanation.surface: A climber gives a nasty look near the summit and decides to turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' turns LEER upside down to REEL, which then wraps around the first letter of peak.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel attackers is to drive them back, forcing them to retreat from where they came.

clue.text: Report unbridled passion about English pieces to be played?

indicators.note: unbridled means unrestrained, running wild, so the letters break loose
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
ire is anger, a passion
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about English fury running wild at a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passion' here is anger, not love; the jumbled letters then go around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A repertoire is the stock of works a musician or company knows and can perform.

clue.text: Excuse to jump quietly to the front

indicators.note: sending a letter to the front moves it from the end round to the start

blocks.note: to jump is to leap
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly; it names the letter of the leap that moves

explanation.surface: A pretext for sneaking forward to the head of a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: The P already at the end of LEAP is the one that moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an appeal or justification offered, which is what an excuse amounts to.

clue.text: Stitch up second person in France, certain to accept that

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: tu is French for you, the second person
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone framed in France is sure to put up with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch up' tempts as slang for framing someone; here it is literal sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: To suture is to sew a wound closed with stitches, a medical verb.

clue.text: Snatched look in practice area when coming round

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it
coming round means turning about to face the other way

blocks.note: the nets are where cricketers practise batting and bowling
lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: A quick glance taken during training as someone turns around.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the nets are netted lanes for practice; LO sits inside them and the lot turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Snatched and stolen are both past participles meaning taken without permission.
